_why: mp:L1. `_only` INVERTS the usual mask: instead of blanking a machine-specific region, it compares ONE rectangle and nothing else. The rectangle is the connection indicator's first line up to but NOT including its digits -- `PING [####]`, measured off the blessed frame at ink columns 740..794 on rows 8..17 -- which is everything about the element whose correct value is fixed: that it is drawn at all, right-aligned in the map viewport's top-right corner (L1d geometry -- WindowWidth/G_WIN_W at this 1024x768 resolution place the reserved column's left edge at x=740; a different resolution places it differently, which is why the position is computed, not hardcoded), in the game's own FONTY08 face, and that the stability bar reads FULL on a clean loopback link. The whole frame outside it is deliberately not compared; match_launch already owns the in-game frame as a whole. RE-CUT 2026-09-18 (L1d): the indicator moved from a fixed `8,44` top-left position (itself a stopgap after the ORIGINAL `8,8` default overprinted retail's own top-left chat/alert line, chat_glyphs) to this geometry-computed top-right one; the rect is keyed to the new position and is resolution-specific to this baseline's 1024x768 capture. RE-CUT 2026-09-22 (mp:L1g): the PING line gained a relay-vs-direct letter BEFORE its digits, so reserved_width() grew by `R ` and the whole right-anchored block moved LEFT by exactly 12 px at this resolution (measured: the `PING` ink starts at 728 where it started at 740, while the digits at 802 and the `ms` at 813..822 did not move -- the anchor is the right edge). Both rects therefore shift by -12, and the n1_hud one ALSO WIDENS 60 -> 72 so the letter is INSIDE the compared region. That widening is the point of the re-cut, not a side effect: the old rect stopped short of the digits, and a rect that stopped short of the LETTER too would leave the suite blind to the very element this row added -- the mp:L1e lobby cell hit exactly that trap with its own digit mask. `D` here is a real measurement, not a default: the host bridge reports relayed=0 because no tunnel is running on a loopback lane (see the run's `; [netind] peer0 ... relayed=0` line), and an unclassifiable transport (-1) draws no letter at all, which keeps a pre-L1g module's frame byte-identical.
_why_not_the_digits: They cannot be baselined and pretending otherwise would bless a lie. The ping differs on every run (it is an RFC 6298 estimate of a live path) and the command-latency number moves with the T3 adaptive lookahead. They are asserted instead by this scenario's post_check, tools/check_net_indicator.py, off the `; [netind]` lines -- a measured srtt, a bar level in range, and cmd_ms == look_ms + step_ms. The digits sit at x >= 802, clear of the rect, BECAUSE the seam puts the varying number last on the line and reserves a fixed-width column for the WHOLE line (measured from a worst-case template, ui_net_indicator.cpp's reserved_width()) rather than right-aligning the live string -- so the label+bar's start column does not drift with the digit count between runs, which is what keeps this rect meaningful across runs at all.
_why_ink_mode: The text is drawn through llm_gfx_draw_text_blend_clipped, i.e. BLENDED with whatever is behind it. The rect sits on the black out-of-map corner and so is stable today, but an ink-threshold compare makes the assertion about the GLYPH SHAPES rather than about the exact blend -- shape still counts, so a missing line or a substituted box fails, while a background that shifts a few levels does not.
_why_n1_stall: mp:TL-UISTALL. `capture_n1_stall.png` is the `stalled 400` frame (mp_client_hud.txt) -- the same PING/CMD block plus a THIRD line, `WAITING FOR <name>`. Its `_only` rect covers `WAITING FOR` (ink columns 740..799 on rows 26..32) and stops BEFORE the peer name for the same reason the PING rect stops before the ping digits: the name is a value, not a fixed label, and belongs to the post_check (`--expect-stall`), not to a pixel compare. It happens to be deterministic in this scenario (the client always waits on the host, so the name is always `host`), but the rect does not rely on that -- it never includes the name pixels at all.
_flake_watch: The bar is the one compared element with a LIVE input: it reads [####] only while IPDV is <= 5 ms and loss <= 5 per mille. Measured ipdv_ms=0 on every sample of every clean local-lane run so far (2026-09-18), which is why tol 0 is honest here rather than hopeful -- but this runs on loopback beside up to eight other game processes under --jobs, so if this capture ever goes red with a bar of [###.] and the post_check green, read it as the BOX being loaded, not as a regression, and say so before reblessing.
_why_rect_height: 9 rows, not 11: the CMD line starts on the row right under the PING line (line height 10 at FONTY08), so an 11-row rect reaches the CMD digits' top row, and CMD grows from 2 to 3 digits under load (the adaptive lookahead) -- measured 0.455% red on a loaded box, 2026-09-18. The rect must stop above the second line.
